findings.title: Cancelling an active generation releases the serial queue while inference continues in a thread
findings.evidence: cancel_generation calls running_task.cancel(). The worker awaits only the asyncio task (49-56), while backend/backends/pytorch_backend.py:243, mlx_backend.py:262 and other engines await asyncio.to_thread(_generate_sync). Cancelling that await does not stop an already-running thread. run_generation catches CancelledError and returns (generation.py:137-144), allowing the queue to launch the next job.
findings.impact: Cancelling a long running generation while another is queued causes overlapping inference on the same shared backend/model, defeating the stated GPU serialization guarantee. Extra GPU memory use, model contention and changed random seeds are credible consequences; actual GPU failure was not tested.
findings.recommendation: Keep exclusive inference ownership until the underlying thread completes, or implement cooperative model cancellation that confirms computation has stopped before advancing the queue. Apply the same ownership guard to unqueued synchronous/stream generation paths.
findings.validation: Reproduced with the real task_queue module and two jobs: first calls asyncio.to_thread on a blocking threading.Event, then is cancelled; second starts before the event is released. /workspace/review/voicebox_repro.py asserts this overlap. Existing cancellation tests use cancellable asyncio.Event waits and do not exercise threaded inference. Stronger independent challenge: /workspace/review/voicebox_production_cancellation_repro.py executes unchanged AST-extracted production run_generation and PyTorchTTSBackend.generate bodies plus the actual generate_chunked and task_queue modules, substituting a blocking model and DB/audio I/O only. It proves first generation writes failed and closes DB, and second generation completes, before the first model thread is released. Frontend reachability: HistoryTable.tsx:468-469 treats generating/loading_model as active; :624-631 offers Cancel generation button; :104-105 invokes apiClient.cancelGeneration; api/client.ts:267-270 posts the production cancel endpoint. No native GUI click was performed.

findings.title: A custom data directory below an ancestor named data breaks saved audio paths
findings.evidence: to_storage_path searches the first path component named data (67-69) before attempting to relativize against the actual configured _data_dir. For _data_dir=/tmp/.../data/voicebox, a newly generated /tmp/.../data/voicebox/generations/example.wav becomes voicebox/generations/example.wav; resolve_storage_path then resolves it to /tmp/.../data/voicebox/voicebox/generations/example.wav.
findings.impact: Valid --data-dir configurations such as /mnt/data/voicebox cause generated audio, samples, captures and avatars to be written successfully but saved under paths that fail on retrieval. Audio endpoints return 404 and profiles cannot reload reference audio.
findings.recommendation: First make paths relative to the configured _data_dir. Limit legacy rebasing by a data-named ancestor to legacy reads/migration, after checking the real configured root.
findings.validation: Executed a stdlib-only round trip with config.set_data_dir(temp/data/voicebox), wrote a temporary generation file, and verified resolve_storage_path(to_storage_path(file)) != file. Reproduction is in /workspace/review/voicebox_repro.py.

findings.title: Omitting engine overrides the selected voice profile default with qwen
findings.evidence: GenerationRequest.engine is Optional but defaults to qwen. routes/generations.py:54-55 resolves data.engine or profile.default_engine or profile.preset_engine, so the profile fallbacks are unreachable for an omitted engine. For a Kokoro preset, validate_profile_engine rejects the unintended qwen value (services/profiles.py:124-134). Both /generate and /generate/stream use this resolver.
findings.impact: API clients sending the documented minimal profile_id/text request cannot use Kokoro or Qwen CustomVoice preset profiles without explicitly supplying engine or null. A cloned profile with a different default engine also uses qwen silently, potentially loading the wrong model.
findings.recommendation: Default GenerationRequest.engine to None, retaining qwen as the final fallback in the route resolver. Test requests omitting engine for both preset and cloned profiles with a configured default.
findings.validation: Instantiated the actual GenerationRequest with no engine and confirmed engine == qwen; applying the route resolver expression to a kokoro default resolves qwen. No inference was needed. Reproduction is in /workspace/review/voicebox_repro.py.

findings.title: Stream generation silently discards the voice profile effects chain
findings.evidence: stream_speech gets profile from services.profiles.get_profile, which returns _profile_to_response (profiles.py:277). That converts stored effects JSON into List[EffectConfig] (profiles.py:35-42; models.py:39). The stream fallback calls json.loads(profile.effects_chain), catches the resulting TypeError, and sets effects_chain_config=None.
findings.impact: POST /generate/stream without an explicit request effects_chain always ignores enabled profile default effects, while persisted /generate correctly loads effects from the database JSON. Streaming audio does not match the configured voice.
findings.recommendation: Use [effect.model_dump() for effect in profile.effects_chain] for the already-deserialized response, or share effects resolution with the persisted generation flow.
findings.validation: Constructed an actual VoiceProfileResponse with enabled reverb EffectConfig and verified the exact json.loads operation raises TypeError because the value is a list. The route catches this and skips apply_effects. Reproduction is in /workspace/review/voicebox_repro.py.

critical_flows: History active row -> Cancel generation button -> apiClient.cancelGeneration -> POST /generate/{id}/cancel -> task_queue.cancel_generation -> Task.cancel -> run_generation CancelledError cleanup. The model thread continues unless explicitly joined/cooperatively stopped.

POST /generate -> Pydantic GenerationRequest -> profile response -> engine resolver/validator -> queue -> run_generation -> generate_chunked -> engine.generate -> asyncio.to_thread -> save version/audio -> generation terminal status.
Written audio path -> config.to_storage_path -> SQLite audio_path -> config.resolve_storage_path -> audio route is_file guard -> FileResponse.
POST /generate/stream -> get_profile returns parsed EffectConfig list -> generation -> request/profile effects resolution -> apply_effects -> optional normalization -> WAV response.

immediate_mitigations.action: Let active model inference finish; cancel only queued work while this defect remains open. After an active cancellation has already occurred, do not submit/retry more generation merely because its row is failed; wait for actual model activity to finish, or fully stop and restart the backend before resuming.
immediate_mitigations.limits: This is an operational workaround, not a code guarantee. Failed UI status does not prove its thread has stopped. Restarting interrupts other clients and queued work. No new configuration flag or safe immediate thread-stop API was found or used.

immediate_mitigations.action: For fresh isolated deployments choose a data root without an earlier ancestor component literally named data, such as /srv/voicebox-store. Before changing any existing deployment location, make a consistent backup of SQLite and the complete data directory and inventory current stored paths.
immediate_mitigations.limits: Changing the root does not repair already-malformed rows. Do not bulk rename/move/delete existing audio or rewrite database paths without a verified mapping and backup. The normal final data directory named data works when no earlier ancestor named data takes precedence.

immediate_mitigations.action: API callers can explicitly supply the engine matching the profile, or explicitly send engine: null to activate the current resolver fallback.
immediate_mitigations.limits: Every caller must apply this workaround. Omission still selects qwen until the request default changes. Explicit engine/profile mismatches should continue to be rejected.

immediate_mitigations.action: Send the intended effects_chain explicitly in streaming requests, or use the persisted /generate flow when profile default effects are required.
immediate_mitigations.limits: Callers must keep the explicit chain synchronized with profile settings. An empty list intentionally disables effects; null or omission currently reaches the broken default fallback. No inference was performed to compare audio perceptually.

findings.recommended_implementation: Retain and join actual threaded model work when the async request is cancelled. Keep the generation queue/resource owner occupied until computation has terminated. Use cooperative engine stopping only where its completion can be proved; otherwise allow the current call to finish before propagating cancellation.
repair_steps: Introduce a maintained fake-model regression that blocks inside the synchronous inference function. Queue a second real generation coroutine, cancel the first, and assert the second model call has not started until the blocked first model finishes.

At each supported inference adapter boundary, retain a handle to the offloaded task and prevent cancellation of the await from losing ownership of the running thread. Defer CancelledError propagation until the thread operation is joined or a cooperative engine stop has actually completed.
Make cancellation cleanup robust against repeated cancel requests and shutdown cancellation. A second Task.cancel must not bypass the join/resource lease.

Keep the existing immediate endpoint acknowledgement semantics if desired: Generation cancellation requested can return while cleanup waits. Only terminalize/advance the generation worker after the resource is no longer executing.
Do not treat awaiting an already-cancelled asyncio task as a thread join. The worker currently sees completion while the detached thread still runs.

Audit threaded model loading/voice-prompt creation and direct stream/nonpersisted generation for resource ownership using the same approach. Limit any broader serialization change to a documented contract rather than silently relying on the queued path to cover unqueued work.
Retain existing queued-cancel behavior: skip and close a not-yet-started coroutine, clear task tracking, and leave the worker usable.
invariants: Cancelling the Python await must not allow a second call to use a shared model/GPU resource while the first synchronous call still owns it.
Every queued job is accounted for exactly once; task_done, tracked generation IDs and task-manager completion remain consistent.
Cancelled generations never persist completed audio after they are declared terminally failed.
Queue progression, model unload and shutdown must respect actual computation lifetime, not merely asyncio Task.done().
Cancellation must not deadlock on exceptions raised by the model or status persistence.
acceptance_criteria: The blocked-thread test shows no overlap and no second model entry until first computation exits, after one or multiple cancellation requests.
The real run_generation cleanup does not record terminal cancellation/release ownership ahead of the selected cancellation contract.
Queued cancellation still prevents model execution and later jobs run successfully.
Model exception during cancellation and status-write failure leave no indefinitely occupied worker/resource lease.
On at least one supported GPU backend, cancelling an active job and immediately queuing another produces no overlapping model calls or unbounded extra GPU memory attributable to overlap.
regression_cases: Cancel before worker starts; cancel during model load; cancel during reference prompt creation; cancel during short and multi-chunk generation.
Cancel twice during a blocked inference; cancel again during cancellation cleanup.
First model raises after cancellation; DB terminal-status write raises; shutdown occurs during inference.
Queue another job and retry the cancelled row; ensure jobs execute serially and IDs/task counts do not leak.
Exercise PyTorch and MLX boundary behavior with deterministic fakes; smoke-test other adapters using the same helper/contract.
Confirm direct /generate/stream and nonpersisted speak calls cannot invalidate the promised resource ownership policy.
compatibility_risks: Without cooperative engine stopping, visible cancellation may remain pending until a long noninterruptible model call returns. This delay is intentional if required to preserve exclusive ownership.
New locking must cover the real model resource and avoid acquiring locks in conflicting order during model load/unload.
Thread joining during shutdown may extend exit time; process watchdog and desktop sidecar lifecycle require explicit validation.
A new cancelling status would affect frontend/MCP consumers and database conventions; preserve existing statuses unless a coordinated contract change is needed.

rollback.code: Revert the inference ownership patch and its dependent UI/status changes together. No schema migration is required for the recommended minimal approach.
rollback.operational_fallback: Return to the active-cancel avoidance workaround. A code rollback restores the original overlap risk; do not label the defect closed.
rollback.data: Use disposable data for cancellation experiments. No production data rewrite is part of this repair.

repair_steps: Add a matrix of config round-trip tests for the default root, a custom root with no data component, a root below an earlier data ancestor, and repeated data components.
In to_storage_path, prioritize resolved_path.relative_to(_data_dir) for current in-root files. Retain an explicit documented fallback for any intentionally supported external absolute paths.
Review resolve_storage_path absolute handling so an existing path under the actual configured root is not mistaken for a legacy path based on an earlier data component.

Keep support for known 0.3.0 relative data/profiles/... rows and supported historical absolute data paths using tested read rules. Reject ambiguity rather than silently selecting a different existing audio file.

Inventory actual malformed persisted rows before proposing recovery. Where a unique existing target can be proven, plan an idempotent mapping with old/new values recorded and a dry-run mode; preserve all audio files.
Run endpoint-level file retrieval tests on a temporary SQLite database after path serialization. Confirm file existence, not just string equality.

None and empty paths remain None; failed generations and directory-valued paths continue returning 404.
Legacy normalization must not overwrite audio, delete files, escape into an unintended storage root, or select a different file based only on a matching basename.
Repairing new writes alone must not be presented as having recovered every existing malformed row.

None, empty string, Path("") and a stored directory remain non-file cases.
Legacy data/profiles/id/sample.wav; known previous absolute root; an external absolute file if the existing contract intentionally permits it.
Both a legacy rebase candidate and an original absolute file exist: do not silently serve the wrong one.

findings.title: Stream generation silently discards the voice profile effects chain
findings.evidence: stream_speech gets profile from services.profiles.get_profile, which returns _profile_to_response (profiles.py:277). That converts stored effects JSON into List[EffectConfig] (profiles.py:35-42; models.py:39). The stream fallback calls json.loads(profile.effects_chain), catches the resulting TypeError, and sets effects_chain_config=None.
findings.impact: POST /generate/stream without an explicit request effects_chain always ignores enabled profile default effects, while persisted /generate correctly loads effects from the database JSON. Streaming audio does not match the configured voice.
findings.validation_already_performed: Constructed an actual VoiceProfileResponse with enabled reverb EffectConfig and verified the exact json.loads operation raises TypeError because the value is a list. The route catches this and skips apply_effects. Reproduction is in /workspace/review/voicebox_repro.py.
affected_workflows: POST /generate/stream relying on profile effects defaults
API clients expecting streamed and saved voice effects to agree

change_surface.purpose: Effects precedence and serialization for streamed WAV generation
Profile response is already parsed into EffectConfig instances
Response effects type and explicit-request override contract
Persisted generation effects behavior used for parity checks
Consumer expects serialized effect dictionaries; inspect validation/application behavior before changing caller

findings.recommended_implementation: Use the typed profile effects list directly, serializing each EffectConfig with model_dump rather than passing the list through json.loads. Preserve request override, explicit empty-list disablement and no-effects semantics.
repair_steps: Add a streaming route regression where get_profile returns a real VoiceProfileResponse with enabled default effects and apply_effects is instrumented.
Replace the erroneous JSON parse of profile.effects_chain with serialization from its typed objects. Keep JSON parsing at the DB/profile-conversion boundary only.
Preserve data.effects_chain is not None as the override check so an explicit empty list disables profile defaults.
Verify enabled/disabled flags and params survive serialization and effects are applied once before the currently established normalization step.
If sharing a small effects-resolution helper with persisted generation, keep it limited to precedence/type conversion. Do not fold in unrelated synthesis or versioning refactors.
invariants: Profile effects defaults are applied when request effects are omitted/null and a valid default chain exists.
Explicit request effects override profile defaults; explicit [] means no effects.
No effects are applied more than once, and parameter values/order/enablement are preserved.
Corrupt stored JSON remains handled at the profile deserialization boundary; the route must not silently swallow a type-contract programming error.
acceptance_criteria: Streaming endpoint calls apply_effects with the expected profile chain when no request override is supplied.
Explicit request chain replaces the profile chain and [] skips application.
Profile with no default effects still streams valid WAV without invoking effect processing.
For deterministic fake inference, persisted and streamed flows resolve the same effective chain; real audio smoke test confirms the intended audible result.
regression_cases: Profile effects None/empty/one enabled effect/multiple ordered effects with mixed enabled flags.
Request chain omitted/null/explicit chain/explicit empty list.
Effect parameters contain supported scalar values and survive model_dump unchanged.
Normalization on/off preserves established processing order and valid WAV response headers.
Malformed legacy profile effects JSON is handled by existing profile conversion behavior, not accidentally reintroduced into the stream parser.
compatibility_risks: Streaming output will intentionally change for voices whose default effects were previously ignored.
Effects can alter duration, amplitude or timbre; preserve existing processing order and validate clipping/normalization with representative audio.
A generalized helper should not reinterpret [] as missing or mutate the profile/request chain.

rollback.code: Revert the stream effects-resolution patch if required; this restores the known missing-effects behavior and does not close the finding.
rollback.fallback: Send effects explicitly or use persisted /generate.
rollback.data: No profile DB or generated audio migration is required; do not rewrite existing files.

reproduction_and_validation.name: Actual tracker threshold probe
prerequisites: Python 3.12 and uv; current probe environment used huggingface-hub 2.2.0 and tqdm 4.70.1
reproduction_and_validation.command:
PYTHONPATH=/workspace/repos/voicebox/backend:/workspace/repos/voicebox uv run --no-project --with pytest --with pytest-asyncio --with sqlalchemy --with fastapi --with httpx --with tqdm --with huggingface-hub python - <<'PYCODE'
from importlib.metadata import version
from backend.utils.hf_progress import HFProgressTracker
print('huggingface-hub', version('huggingface-hub'), 'tqdm', version('tqdm'))
for size in (1000, 2000000):
    reports = []
    tracker = HFProgressTracker(lambda *args: reports.append(args))
    with tracker.patch_download():
        from tqdm import tqdm
        with tqdm(total=size, desc='model.bin', unit='B', disable=True) as progress:
            progress.update(size)
    print('Total bytes:', size, 'callback count:', len(reports))
PYCODE
reproduction_and_validation.limits: No download or model inference takes place. The tracker force-enables its own accounting, so a terminal progress display can still appear despite disable=True in the probe.
